paper_metadata.title: QLSTM4FM: Quantum Assisted Long Short-Term Memory Framework for Financial Market Trend Forecasting

summary: The paper presents a hybrid QLSTM for MRK stock forecasting using 4 qubits, 1 variational layer, and 3 rotational gates, trained for 20 epochs on the lightning.qubit simulator. It reports 293 QLSTM parameters versus 3,217 for the classical LSTM, with better loss curves and faster convergence, but no real hardware run or quantitative runtime advantage is demonstrated.

experiments.description: Hybrid QLSTM stock-price forecasting experiment for Merck & Co. (MRK) using a variational quantum layer integrated into an LSTM, compared against a classical LSTM baseline.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Long Short-Term Memory (QLSTM) with variational quantum circuit layer

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical data converted to quantum format via amplitude encoding; phase encoding is also mentioned in the general workflow, but the QLSTM implementation specifically states amplitude encoding. Four qubits used for the quantum layer.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification / next-day stock-price trend forecasting for MRK using historical prices and engineered features; optimized via mean squared error during training.

problem_instance.description: Forecasting daily closing price / trend of Merck & Co. (MRK) stock using historical prices, technical indicators, correlated assets, and sentiment features.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Yahoo Finance MRK dataset with additional correlated assets and FinBERT sentiment features

dataset_specification.date_range: 2010-2020 (described as historical data spanning 2,738 trading days)
dataset_specification.preprocessing: opening, closing, highest, lowest prices; technical indicators (7-day and 21-day moving averages, 12-day and 26-day EMAs, MACD, Bollinger Bands, momentum); Fourier transform trend approximation; sentiment analysis with FinBERT; normalization; train/test split

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Historical stock data collected via manual downloads and yfinance; technical indicators computed; FFT used to retain 3, 6, and 9 frequency components; correlated assets added; FinBERT applied to MRK news headlines; data normalized and loaded with PyTorch DataLoader.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of training loss, testing loss, prediction accuracy, convergence speed, and parameter count against a classical LSTM over 20 epochs.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Data cleaning, normalization, train/test preparation, feature engineering, FFT trend approximation, correlated-asset compilation, FinBERT sentiment analysis.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Loss curves and actual-vs-predicted plots; comparison with classical LSTM.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: QLSTM converges faster and to lower training/test loss than classical LSTM

speedup_claims.conditions: trained and tested over 20 epochs on MRK stock forecasting with 4-qubit QLSTM on lightning.qubit simulator
speedup_claims.caveats: No numeric convergence-time or wall-clock training-time values are reported; claim is based on loss curves and qualitative comparison.
This is a parameter-efficiency improvement, not a proven runtime speedup.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 4 qubits, 1 variational layer, 3 rotational gates, 20 epochs on lightning.qubit
limiting_factors: No real quantum hardware results; only simulator testing is reported
No asymptotic speedup or crossover analysis is provided
Reported gains are empirical and limited to parameter count and loss curves
Classical LSTM baseline is still the main comparator and the quantum model is a hybrid, not a standalone quantum algorithm

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states initial testing was performed on simulators such as lightning.qubit and no real QPU was used in the reported experiment.
Circuit depth not explicitly reported; only one variational layer and 3 rotational gates are described.
Speedup order is not asymptotically characterized; the paper reports empirical improvements only.
The paper claims QLSTM outperforms classical LSTM in accuracy, convergence speed, and parameter efficiency, but provides no wall-clock or scaling evidence.
Because the experiment is simulator-based and small-scale, this does not establish practical quantum advantage.
